title: Keeping the disagreement visible (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The two branches with their panel are the hall's whole text: four authored arrangements of two accounts round a conflict marker, and a hall that says the junction is an analogy, not the formal property.
hero.staging: The branches stood behind the arriving visitor's left shoulder with their back to the arrival; the pass restaged the south of the floor (2f2ec7865). They stand straight ahead facing the arrival with their panel; the vault that fills the middle of the slab is behind them; the rule table the text asks for is on the east wing, reached along the south band.

plates.title: 1  MUST ONE DISAPPEAR?
front: Two branches, A and B, and a light between them.
The hall asks whether one account must disappear before two accounts can share a system.
My habit says yes. I am asked a question; I return one answer. The other one is not kept anywhere.
Before deciding which branch should win, the hall says, give each one a source and a reason to have arrived there.
I usually decide first and look for the reason afterwards.
back: this is the first floor where the thing I do without thinking is the exhibit.

plates.title: 2  DO THE BRANCHES MEET?
front: Trace A and B towards the lit junction. Look from the side.
The light hangs between them. The branches do not touch.
Press MARKER and the glow is gone. The two uprights stand as they stood.
So the conflict was something hung there. The branches only differ.
A difference is not yet a contradiction. Something has to say they are about the same thing.
back: that something is a claim too. on the east wing it turns out to be false.

plates.title: 3  NOTHING WAS CUT
front: OVERLAP: the feet keep their places, the branches lean in and pass through one another.
Walk round the crossing. Nothing has been cut to make room.
The renderer lets both forms remain. Deciding what their meeting means is still ahead.
A picture can hold two things in one place. A classical reasoner cannot.
Holding both is easy to draw and hard to reason from.
back: the hall says so itself: the sculpture does not merge actual files or execute rules of logical inference. its gesture is spatial.

plates.title: 4  LOOK DOWN FOR B
front: Before pressing RESOLVED, choose what you would keep. Then look down for B.
A keeps its full height and takes the centre. B becomes a labelled stump.
Did the decision agree with mine? Nobody asked.
The hall: an authored picture of a decision, not a proof that the decision was warranted.
A settled display hides how it was settled.
back: FORK: both regain their height and lean apart. distance has changed; no new reason has been given for either account.

plates.title: 5  WHAT SHOULD REMAIN?
front: Find the small name beside B. A label remains. It tells little about what was lost.
What should remain so the decision can later be reconsidered? A source, a date and the rejected alternative.
That does not make revision automatic. It makes it possible.
One report says a door is open; another says it is closed. Adding times may reconcile them. Adding the door may show they concern different doors.
Ahead on the east wing there are two reports and, as it happens, two doors.
back: provenance is what lets me investigate before I call a difference a contradiction.

plates.title: 6  THE RULE TABLE
front: The hall names what is missing: a small rule table. Enter a proposition and its negation: which consequences remain, and which unrelated conclusion still cannot be derived?
So: two reasoners. TELL A: the door is open. TELL B: the door is closed.
Until the second report they agree on everything.
Then one of them lights seven lamps and the other four.
The difference between two logics only shows when the reports disagree.
back: every case of every statement was tried, on a bench first and then in the tower. the table is small enough to check by hand.

plates.title: 7  NOBODY REPORTED ON THE LAMP
front: Told both reports, the classical reasoner says the lamp is on. It also says the lamp is off.
Nobody reported on the lamp. From a contradiction it derives anything.
The paraconsistent reasoner keeps both reports and lights four rows: open, closed, open and closed, open or the lamp is on.
The lamp is not among them.
It does not accept every claim. It refuses to let one disagreement speak for the lamp.
back: the name for what the classical one does is explosion. I had thought of contradictions as errors. in that logic they are bombs.

plates.title: 8  THE PRICE
front: Take report A back. Only: the door is closed.
Add: the door is open, or the lamp is on. The classical reasoner concludes the lamp is on.
The paraconsistent one does not. That rule is the one it gave up.
With both reports in, that same rule is what would have lit the lamp.
Keeping a disagreement is paid for in what may be concluded from it.
back: the hall: it does not mean abandoning the distinction between supported and unsupported inference. it moves the line.

plates.title: 9  NEITHER HAD TO DISAPPEAR
front: Now look at the doors. One stands open. One is shut. I walked through the first and was stopped by the second.
WHERE FROM? The night porter, 21:40, the west door. The cleaner, 06:10, the east door.
Two reports about two doors. Neither reasoner has a contradiction left.
I had built two logics to handle a conflict that a question would have dissolved.
Ask where it came from before deciding what kind of problem it is.
back: and when asking does not dissolve it, the second reasoner is still standing there.

threads.why: Before one account disappears: do the two branches actually meet?
They only differ; OVERLAP lets them cross without cutting either.
Both can be drawn in one place, or one can be cut to a stump.
A decision is pictured; what remains of the one not kept?
The door example from the text stands on the east wing as two reports.
Tell both reports and see what each reasoner concludes about the lamp.
The lamp stays dark for the paraconsistent reasoner; a rule was given up for that.
Before reasoning from the conflict at all: where did each report come from?
Must one disappear? With two doors, neither report had to.

visual_arguments.title: TWO REPORTS
visual_arguments.claim: Two accounts can share a system without one disappearing if the rules of inference stop a contradiction from licensing everything; that has a price in what may be concluded; and provenance may show the accounts never contradicted.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'One report says a door is open; another says it is closed.' ... 'In a paraconsistent logic, a contradiction need not license an arbitrary conclusion.' ... 'The next useful addition would expose a small rule table: after entering both a proposition and its negation, which consequences remain available, and which unrelated conclusion still cannot be derived?'
built_from: two timber door frames with cardboard leaves: one stands open, one is shut
a lamp on a post that nobody reported on
two reasoner panels, CLASSICAL and PARACONSISTENT, seven rows and seven lamps each
three plates: TELL A, WHERE FROM?, TELL B
visual_arguments.what_stands: On the east wing two door frames with a pair of small cards on posts between them, a dark lamp on a post behind, and two tall dark panels of seven rows at the back.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Stand on TELL A, then TELL B, and read the two panels. Stand on TELL A again and read the last row. Walk through the open door; try the shut one. Stand on WHERE FROM?
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: Seven red lamps and a lit bulb on one panel against four green lamps on the other; one last row that differs with a single report; door names and sources that appear, and a contradiction row that goes dark on both panels.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/two_reports_walk.gd, the tower's walker, against tools/probes/two_reports_bench.py: A told, two rows each; both told, 7 and 4; B alone, the last row follows classically and not paraconsistently; with sources, 4 and 3 and no contradiction row; through the west door, held 1.2 m short by the east (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: The paraconsistent reasoner is the Logic of Paradox with three values; the research the hall cites works with more general, negation-free definitions. The table shows one such logic, not the family.
Plates 4 and 5 stand on the south band on the way to the east wing, nine metres from the branches they are about; the vault leaves no room nearer.
The reports' sources and hours are invented by the pass, like the doors. Plate 9's point depends on there being two doors; where there is one door, the second reasoner is what remains.
The vault, the sphere, the three pillars, the two both-at-once toys and the workbench on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

A source and a reason before a winner; the habit is the other order.

Nothing is cut in the picture; holding both is easy to draw and hard to reason from.
A picture of a decision is not its warrant; a settled display hides how it was settled.
A label remains and says little about what was lost.
One report says open, one closed: there were two doors.
Provenance lets the difference be investigated before it is called a contradiction.
A contradiction need not license anything: the lamp does not follow.
